answer: Decaying Activity Bond**: Each identity posts a small refundable deposit that decays with inactivity and must be topped up to keep transacting, so idle sybils bleed value over time. Honest agents offset this through steady use; attackers pay a rising per-identity holding cost that compounds like a slow spiral across thousands of accounts. Agents also gain a persistent reputation weight that a fresh cluster lacks, making each new identity a walnut-sized seed requiring long cultivation before it can act. The ocean of honest liquidity drowns cheap clones.
